name: Roti
summary: Soft, flaky flatbread made by coiling buttered dough into layers, rolled thin and pan-fried, for tearing and scooping up curry.
about: Roti is the everyday bread of both Cape Malay and Durban Indian homes, made to go with curries, dhal and bean dishes, and rolled around curry as a 'salomie' in Cape Town. The South African style is soft and layered: the dough is spread with butter, rolled up into a coil and rested before rolling out, and the cooked roti is clapped between the hands to open the layers.

ingredients.name: Lukewarm water
ingredients.note: you may need a little more

ingredients.name: Melted butter and oil
ingredients.note: mixed half and half, for frying

steps: Mix the flour and salt in a large bowl. Add the oil and most of the water and mix with your hand into a soft dough, adding the rest of the water a spoonful at a time if dry flour remains.
Knead on a lightly floured surface for 5 minutes until smooth and stretchy, like soft earlobe. Cover with a damp cloth and rest for 20 minutes so the gluten relaxes.
Divide into 8 equal balls. On a lightly oiled surface, roll one ball into a very thin circle, about 25 cm across, and spread it thinly with soft butter.

Roll the circle up tightly into a long sausage, then coil the sausage into a flat spiral like a snail shell, tucking the end underneath. Repeat with the rest, cover and rest for 20 minutes (or refrigerate for up to a day).
Heat a large heavy frying pan or flat griddle over medium-high heat for 3 minutes. Roll a coil out thinly into a 20 cm circle without pressing too hard, so the layers stay separate.

Cook the roti for about 1 minute until bubbles appear and the underside has golden spots. Turn, brush the top with the butter-and-oil mix, turn again and brush the other side, cooking 30–60 seconds a side until golden-spotted and cooked through with no doughy patches.
Lift it off and, while still hot, scrunch or clap it between your hands to open up the flaky layers. Stack the cooked roti in a clean tea towel to keep them soft while you cook the rest.
prepNote: Coil the dough up to a day ahead and refrigerate; cooked roti freeze well between sheets of baking paper.
